# iothub_query (Data Source)

Runs an [IoT Hub query language](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/iot-hub/iot-hub-devguide-query-language) statement against the hub and returns all results.

The query index is eventually consistent: a new device is visible a few seconds after creation, and a deleted device can be listed for a while afterwards. For a single known device, prefer the `iothub_device` or `iothub_device_twin` data source.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Device IDs and rings of every device in the Munich site (a projection,
# item_type "Raw").
data "iothub_query" "munich" {
  query = <<-EOT
    SELECT deviceId, tags.fleet.ring AS ring FROM devices
    WHERE tags.site = 'munich'
  EOT
}

locals {
  munich_devices = [
    for row in data.iothub_query.munich.results : jsondecode(row).deviceId
  ]
}

# Whole twins (item_type "Twin").
data "iothub_query" "stale_firmware" {
  query = <<-EOT
    SELECT * FROM devices
    WHERE properties.reported.firmware.version
      != properties.desired.firmware.version
  EOT
}

output "stale_firmware_count" {
  value = length(data.iothub_query.stale_firmware.results)
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `query` (String) The statement, for example `SELECT deviceId, tags.site FROM devices WHERE tags.fleet.region = 'eu'`.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) A short hash of the query.
- `item_type` (String) The kind of result rows as reported by the hub: `Raw` for a projection, `Twin` for `SELECT * FROM devices` or `devices.modules`, `DeviceJob` for `FROM devices.jobs`.
- `results` (List of String) One JSON string per result row, in the order the hub returns them.
